text:
mike_r: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression on the continuous-batcher after rolling the KV cache refactor. Long requests (5k+ tokens) are getting starved while shorts blow through. Profiling attached.
anya: ugh. which commit? :grimacing:
mike_r: commit abc1234, pushed last night. perf-ci alerted ~2:10am. flame link: https://perf.internal/fg/abc1234
mike_r: quick summary from `perf top` — hot path is now `kv_cache::lookup` -> fallback path -> kernel selection stall. Kernel selector blocks waiting for cache hit heuristic, holding batch queue head.
dylan: are we still prioritizing short-only microbatches? I thought we had token-budget targets per tenant.
anya: we do, but the refill algorithm uses `recent_kv_hit_rate` which dropped from 0.87 -> 0.42 for some tenants after refactor. That pushes lots of tokens into long-lane, starving medium-latency short requests.
leah_s: can you paste the batching config you used in prod? maybe the thresholds are too aggressive.
mike_r: here’s the live config (sanitized):

```
batching:
  token_budget_target: 0.55
  credit_refill_ms: 40
  short_seq_threshold_tokens: 128
  lane_weights:
    short: 1.2
    medium: 1.0
    long: 0.7
  kv_hit_smoothing_window_ms: 30000
  kv_miss_penalty: 0.6
```
dylan: kv_miss_penalty reduced cache-bias, but if hits drop a lot short lane sees less refill because short lane depends on prefix-kv hits to avoid long tail.
perf-ci: [alert] regression detected: p99 latency +18% for channel=hosted, model=gptx-1b, window=1h, run=1965432000
mike_r: hypothesis: the kernel selector now defers selecting quantized kernels if `kv_hit_smoothing_window_ms` reports unstable hit_rate, causing a stall while kernel selection tries to match ideal kernel for predicted seq length. That combined with credit refills being tied to kv_hit_rate => head-of-line blocking.
anya: two mitigation ideas:
  1) decouple short-lane credit refills from kv_hit_rate — use local short-lane fallback budget that decays slowly.
  2) allow kernel selector to pick fallback quantized kernel immediately if decision latency > 3ms, rather than waiting for confirmatory stats.
dylan: +1 to both. also add a small preemptive credit injection when queue imbalance crosses threshold (short_queue_len > long_queue_len * 2).
leah_s: we should be careful with preemptive injections — might violate tenant fairness. maybe limit to burst windows per-tenant (e.g., once per 15s).
mike_r: I tried a quick patch on a canary pool: gave short lane a 0.2 token budget floor and forced kernel fallback after 3ms. p99 dropped ~12% in the canary (same traffic). will run longer tests.
anya: please dump a short trace of one starved request (include headers and kernel choices). helps see if kernel selection waited on kv result.
mike_r: pasted minimal trace below:
```
TRACE 1965432145: req=tx9876 tenant=acme model=gptx-1b seq_len=5200
  enqueue -> select_lane(long)
  kv_cache_lookup -> miss (async)
  kernel_selector wait 5.4ms for kv_predict (blocked)
  kernel_selected: fp16_fused after wait
  batch_start -> long microbatch 3 items
  tail latency -> 420ms
```
dylan: blockers: we need a safe rollout plan. if we decouple refill from kv stats we need metrics to ensure long unfairness doesn't creep in.
anya: propose rollout plan:
  - step 0: enable short-floor=0.2 in canary for 2h, collect p50/p95/p99 by tenant
  - step 1: enable immediate kernel-fallback threshold=3ms in canary
  - step 2: enable queue-imbalance probe to inject small credits (0.05) with per-tenant cooldown 15s
  - step 3: if metrics good, ramp to 20% of clusters then 100%
leah_s: also add a regression test in CI simulating KV miss storm + mixed seq lengths. we had no test for that after the refactor.
perf-ci: [note] created perf job: regression-ci/kv-miss-mix-196543
infra-bot: canary pool created: pool-canary-7, nodes=4 g4dnx-large
mike_r: thx. I'll push the short-floor patch now and attach canary logs. pls watch tenant-level fairness dashboards — set alert if any tenant's short_p99 > baseline*1.15
anya: one more thought — consider changing `kv_hit_smoothing_window_ms` to percentile-based smoothing (p50/p90) rather than mean; mean gets skewed by bursts and causes oscillation.
dylan: good call. that might reduce oscillatory refill behavior that causes credit thrash.
mike_r: ok pushing changes. will update thread with canary metrics in ~30m. :pray:
